stonewall_line_reinforcement.name: Line Reinforcement

stonewall_line_reinforcement.designIntent: Choose protection for the enemy response instead of Triage’s larger heal. Armor expires before the next friendly initiative and cannot stop direct removal.

stonewall_reserve_watch.name: Reserve Watch
stonewall_reserve_watch.rulesText: Retaliate — after surviving as combat defender, deal 1 damage to the surviving attacker. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.

stonewall_breach_shield.name: Breach Shield Column
stonewall_breach_shield.rulesText: Armor. Guard. Mobile — first move each turn preserves readiness, keeping interception available after repositioning. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
stonewall_breach_shield.designIntent: Carry a defensive screen through the moving frontline. Pays a Command Action and sacrifices offensive stats for mobile protection.

bruiser_pavise_breaker.name: Pavise Breaker

bruiser_ram_team.name: Armored Ram Team
bruiser_ram_team.rulesText: Armor. Berserk — gain +1 Attack while wounded. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
bruiser_ram_team.designIntent: Commit to a slower, durable breakthrough body rather than raw Heavy damage. Still vulnerable to direct removal, Sabotage and pressure in another position.

bruiser_surge_drummers.name: Surge Drummers
bruiser_surge_drummers.rulesText: Command — other allies here gain +1 Attack. Mobile — first move each turn preserves readiness. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
bruiser_surge_drummers.designIntent: Shift a fragile assault aura between groups. Small Presence commitment comes with an explicit Command Action and almost no independent damage.

bruiser_counterpuncher.name: Counterpuncher

bruiser_triage_rig.name: Combat Triage Rig
bruiser_triage_rig.rulesText: Heal one wounded friendly permanent by 3. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
bruiser_triage_rig.designIntent: Spend a draw slot on preserving an expensive push instead of Resupply. Healing can remove Berserk, creating a timing decision.

bruiser_breakthrough_gunner.name: Breakthrough Gunner
bruiser_breakthrough_gunner.rulesText: Rush — may attack on its deployment turn if ready. Armor — reduce incoming regular combat damage by 1. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
bruiser_breakthrough_gunner.designIntent: Buy a protected deployment-turn shot with higher commitment and lower raw health than Siege Heavy. A 4-damage Order kills this Gunner while an unwounded Siege Heavy survives; deployment, movement and attack can consume the whole initiative.

syndicate_target_designator.name: Target Designator
syndicate_target_designator.rulesText: Mark one enemy permanent: it takes +1 incoming regular combat damage until its next offensive turn starts. Marks do not stack. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
syndicate_target_designator.designIntent: Turn coordinated exchanges into selective removal instead of spending on direct damage. Guard and defensive responses remain available.

syndicate_screen_operator.name: Screen Operator
syndicate_screen_operator.rulesText: Armor. Guard — while ready, intercept an attack on another ally here; Precision bypasses Guard. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
syndicate_screen_operator.designIntent: Protect a marked-target operation without copying Rapid Security Detail’s mobility. Gives up Attack and movement readiness for combat protection.

syndicate_fire_coordinator.name: Fire Coordinator
syndicate_fire_coordinator.rulesText: Command — other allies here gain +1 Attack. Precision — attacks cannot be redirected by Guard. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
syndicate_fire_coordinator.designIntent: Bridge the two tactical archetypes with a fragile aura that can contribute to the selected target. Gives up Coordinator health and Attack for Precision.

syndicate_patch_team.name: Tactical Patch Team
syndicate_patch_team.rulesText: Medic — at your offensive turn start, heal every ally here by 1. Guard — intercept while ready. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
syndicate_patch_team.designIntent: Combine two supporting jobs in one slot while accepting low damage and fragile health. Small direct Orders can remove the combined support.

syndicate_breach_monitor.name: Breach Monitor
syndicate_breach_monitor.rulesText: Armor. Precision — attacks cannot be redirected by Guard. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
syndicate_breach_monitor.designIntent: Offer a durable specialist for planned Mark exchanges instead of an Eliminator’s movement and burst damage. Costs a Command Action to deploy.

syndicate_field_link.name: Field Link
syndicate_field_link.rulesText: Immobile asset. Command — other allies here gain +1 Attack. Medic — at your offensive turn start, heal every ally here by 1. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
syndicate_field_link.designIntent: Combine auras cheaply in Presence while risking a fragile static asset and a Command Action. It cannot follow a breakthrough or retreat after capture.

syndicate_cover_protocol.name: Cover Protocol
syndicate_cover_protocol.rulesText: Reinforce — heal one friendly permanent by 1, then give it temporary Armor 1 until your next offensive turn starts. Does not stack with printed Armor. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
syndicate_cover_protocol.designIntent: Protect the next combined exchange with a small, temporary investment. Sacrifices healing quantity and a deck slot for short-term protection.

nightwalker_exposure_window.name: Exposure Window
nightwalker_exposure_window.rulesText: Mark one enemy permanent: it takes +1 incoming regular combat damage until its next offensive turn starts. Marks do not stack. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
nightwalker_exposure_window.designIntent: Set up a chosen assassination with a visible, short window rather than additional raw stats. Pays more Presence than Syndicate’s specialized targeting tool.

nightwalker_shadow_handler.name: Shadow Handler
nightwalker_shadow_handler.rulesText: Command — other allies here gain +1 Attack. Precision — attacks cannot be redirected by Guard. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
nightwalker_shadow_handler.designIntent: Supply a low-commitment aura for timed disruption and removal. Its tiny independent Attack and health make revealing it a risk.

nightwalker_misfire_team.name: Misfire Team
nightwalker_misfire_team.rulesText: Precision. Retaliate — after surviving as combat defender, deal 1 damage to the surviving attacker. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
nightwalker_misfire_team.designIntent: Choose a unit that discourages enemy cleanup rather than Blade Team’s higher Attack. It has no deployment-turn attack or movement shortcut.

nightwalker_false_route.name: False Route
nightwalker_false_route.rulesText: Add 3 temporary Presence spending to the opponent until their next offensive turn starts. Does not reduce Command Actions. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
nightwalker_false_route.designIntent: Restrict enemy response Capacity during a planned operation without dealing damage. Costs a Command Action and expires when the opponent’s offensive turn starts.

nightwalker_decoy_patrol.name: Decoy Patrol
nightwalker_decoy_patrol.rulesText: Guard. Mobile — first move each turn preserves readiness, keeping interception available. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
nightwalker_decoy_patrol.designIntent: Trade a cheap body and a move for protecting the important operative. Low damage, health and pressure prevent the decoy from becoming a finisher.

nightwalker_route_keeper.name: Route Keeper
nightwalker_route_keeper.rulesText: Guard. Precision — attacks cannot be redirected by Guard. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
nightwalker_route_keeper.designIntent: Let a planned operation defend its support without abandoning selective targeting. Lower Attack than ordinary Nightwalker threats and no Rush.

nightwalker_crossfire_cell.name: Crossfire Cell
nightwalker_crossfire_cell.rulesText: Precision. Mobile. Retaliate — after surviving as combat defender, deal 1 damage to the surviving attacker. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
nightwalker_crossfire_cell.designIntent: Favor flexible positioning and an awkward counterattack over Silencer Team’s immediate burst. No Rush and modest Attack make the timing deliberate.

rogue_field_options.name: Field Options
rogue_field_options.rulesText: Adapt — choose one: Repair (heal one ally by 3); Resupply (draw 2); Reposition (ready one exhausted ally). Every mode costs 1 Command Action. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
rogue_field_options.designIntent: Keep one card useful across different positions. Flexibility costs more tempo than a dedicated heal/draw Order and more Presence than Rally.

rogue_route_scout.name: Route Scout
rogue_route_scout.rulesText: Mobile. Scavenge — when another ally here is destroyed, draw 1 (once per player per turn; sources do not stack). Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
rogue_route_scout.designIntent: Re-establish a cheap salvage network after losses. A fragile body and low capture pressure keep it from replacing durable Broker builds.

rogue_scrap_hauler.name: Scrap Hauler
rogue_scrap_hauler.rulesText: Armor. Scavenge — when another ally here is destroyed, draw 1 (once per player per turn; sources do not stack). Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
rogue_scrap_hauler.designIntent: Maintain recovery value under repeated combat without Bulwark’s interception. Lower Attack and lack of Guard expose the rest of the force.

rogue_field_negotiator.name: Field Negotiator
rogue_field_negotiator.rulesText: Command — other allies here gain +1 Attack. Scavenge — draw 1 when another ally here is destroyed, once per player per turn. Costs 1 Command Action in addition to Capacity.
rogue_field_negotiator.designIntent: Make casualties and coordinated attacks support the same plan. Paying a Command Action for a low-Attack fragile aura prevents free support stacking.

rogue_wandering_medic.name: Salvage Medic
rogue_wandering_medic.rulesText: Medic — at your offensive turn start, heal every ally here by 1. Scavenge — draw 1 when another ally here is destroyed, once per player per turn. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
rogue_wandering_medic.designIntent: Choose whether to preserve allies or accept a casualty for recovery. Loses Repair Courier mobility and health in exchange for salvage value.

rogue_patchguard.name: Patchguard
rogue_patchguard.rulesText: Guard. Armor — reduce incoming regular combat damage by 1 on any ground. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
rogue_patchguard.designIntent: Protect an improvised support group without buying an expensive salvage engine. Modest Attack and no mobility limit aggressive flexibility.

rogue_rolling_cache.name: Salvage Cache
rogue_rolling_cache.rulesText: Immobile asset. Medic — at your offensive turn start, heal every ally here by 1. Scavenge — draw 1 when another ally here is destroyed, once per player per turn. Free Action — costs Capacity; no Command Action.
rogue_rolling_cache.designIntent: Combine healing and recovery in a single slot at the price of fixed deployment. Advancing abandons its support and a lost territory eliminates the cache.

passive.name: Hold Fast
passive.text: At the start of your offensive turn, heal 1 damage from each allied battlefield card in territory you control.

active.name: Lasting Resolve
active.text: Once per match: heal 3 damage from a damaged allied battlefield card and give it temporary Armor 1 until your next offensive turn. Armor does not stack with printed Armor.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Build around Fortify, Guard, durable units and Reinforce. Holding friendly ground lets wounded forces recover.

passive.name: Return Fire
passive.text: An allied unit that survives as the defender in regular combat gains +1 Attack until the end of your next offensive turn. This bonus does not stack.

active.name: Countermand
active.text: Once per match: ready an exhausted allied unit and give it +1 Attack until the end of this offensive turn. This bonus does not stack with Return Fire. Deployment-turn attack restrictions still apply.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose Guard, Retaliate and resilient attackers. Survive enemy pressure, then convert defensive survivors into a controlled counterattack.

passive.name: Drive Forward
passive.text: At your offensive turn end, add 2 extra capture progress if a Rush or Mobile allied unit occupies the contested territory. This is territorial pressure, not spendable Capacity.

active.name: Breach Order
active.text: Once per match: ready an allied unit in the contested territory and give it +2 Attack until this offensive turn ends. Deployment-turn attack restrictions still apply.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose Rush, Mobile and cheap occupation units to establish pressure; commit the signature burst when it can break resistance.

passive.name: Scent of Weakness
passive.text: Your initiated regular combat attacks gain +1 Attack against a wounded enemy. The bonus does not apply to retaliation, direct damage or a target that was fully healed before combat resolves.

active.name: Finish the Hunt
active.text: Once per match: deal 3 direct damage to a wounded enemy battlefield card. Direct damage ignores Armor and Fortify.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose selective damage, Precision and aggressive finishers. Set up wounds before committing elimination attacks.

passive.name: Target Network
passive.text: Your action Orders whose selected effect is Mark cost 1 less Capacity, to a minimum of 1. Printed Presence and all other effects are unchanged.

active.name: Priority Target
active.text: Once per match: Mark an enemy battlefield card and deal 2 direct damage to it. Mark lasts until its owner’s next offensive turn.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose Mark, Precision and coordinated attackers. Spend less on setup, then exploit a visible target with regular combat.

passive.name: Rapid Logistics
passive.text: The first action Order each offensive turn with printed Presence 3 or less and printed Command Action cost above 0 costs 0 Command Actions. Its Capacity cost is unchanged.

active.name: Reserve Release
active.text: Once per match: clear up to 4 temporary spent Capacity and draw 2 cards. Does not release deployed commitment or exceed total Capacity.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose inexpensive tactical Orders, draw support and efficient combined arms. Sequence the free tactical Order before costly commands.

passive.name: Veiled Entry
passive.text: The first Precision unit you deploy each offensive turn gains temporary Armor 1 until your next offensive turn. This does not stack with printed Armor.

active.name: Fade to Shadow
active.text: Once per match: withdraw an allied unit one territory toward home into adjacent friendly ground, heal up to 3 damage and ready it. Destination slots and deployment-turn attack restrictions still apply.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose Precision units and Ambush responses. Protect the first infiltrator, then withdraw a valuable unit before it is overwhelmed.

passive.name: Supply Interference
passive.text: The first Sabotage action Order you resolve each offensive turn also locks 1 enemy available Capacity until their next offensive turn. It cannot lock committed Capacity.

active.name: Blackout
active.text: Once per match: suppress the printed traits of every enemy battlefield card in the contested territory until its owner’s next offensive turn, and lock up to 2 enemy available Capacity for that window.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose Sabotage, selective damage and occupation forces. Disable a frontline’s abilities before attacking; disrupted spending clears at enemy initiative.

passive.name: Nothing Wasted
passive.text: When an allied battlefield card is destroyed, draw 1 card if your casualty-draw allowance is unused. Nothing Wasted and all Scavenge sources share one draw per player per global turn. A surviving nearby Scavenge source receives the trigger instead; the Commander provides salvage elsewhere.

active.name: Recover the Fallen
active.text: Once per match: return the most recent non-Order card in your discard to your hand. Redeployment pays its printed costs and starts without wounds.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose Scavenge, low-cost battlefield units and valuable recovery targets. Trade expendable forces while preserving tools for the next push.

passive.name: Open Route
passive.text: Your first normal unit movement each offensive turn costs 0 Command Actions. Normal adjacency, readiness, slots and movement exhaustion rules still apply.

active.name: Change the Plan
active.text: Once per match: relocate an allied unit to any territory you control or the contested territory, and ready it. Destination slots and deployment-turn attack restrictions still apply.

hook.name: Deckbuilding direction
hook.text: Choose Mobile and Adapt cards plus flexible occupation forces. Save a movement command, then redeploy pressure where the board opens.

glossary.Presence: Every permanent card’s printed P is its deployment requirement, continuing field commitment, and contribution toward capture. Orders spend their printed P temporarily.
glossary.Command: Total Capacity, not Command Actions. Subsequent offensive turns grow Capacity to the configured cap and clear temporary spending.
glossary.Available: Command − Field commitment − temporary spending. Destroyed or reclaimed cards immediately free commitment. Spending refreshes only at the start of your next offensive turn.
glossary.Actions: Command Actions pay for major tactical decisions. Check each card’s command cost; ordinary deployments remain legal at zero Command Actions if Capacity and friendly slots are available.
glossary.Deploy: Deploy into any territory you own with a free friendly slot. New units are ready and may move, but cannot attack that turn without Rush. Assets are immobile.
glossary.Move: A ready unit moves one adjacent territory and exhausts. Destination must be owned or contested; stranded units may take a legal step toward the current objective. There is no jumping over territories.
glossary.Combat: A ready unit attacks an enemy in its territory and exhausts. After one defender response and at most one counter, both surviving participants deal their Attack simultaneously. Wounds persist; cards at zero health enter their owner’s discard.
glossary.Capture: At offensive turn end, surviving cards in the contested territory add printed Presence to capture progress, even with enemies present. At threshold the territory is captured; enemy survivors immediately retreat toward home into adjacent friendly territory or are eliminated. Then the frontline advances and eligible attackers make a Breakthrough.
glossary.Breakthrough: After a non-winning capture, your units and leaders in the captured territory automatically advance one adjacent territory to the new objective, up to its friendly slot limit. Earlier-deployed cards advance first. Wounds and readiness are preserved. Assets and overflow stay behind; this costs no action.
glossary.Conquest: Capture the opponent’s home territory, or reach the configured territory requirement (default all seven). Recapturing an already-owned objective still pushes the front back toward the opponent.
glossary.Response: The defender may play one legal response Order, intercept with a ready Guard here, or pass. A response Order opens one counter opportunity for the attacker. Combat then resolves exactly once.
glossary.Guard: A ready Guard in the same territory can intercept an attack on another friendly card. The Guard exhausts. Precision prevents interception; Guard is not an Order and cannot be countered.
glossary.Fortify: Reduce incoming combat damage by 1 while this card is on a territory its owner controls. Does not reduce Order or Ambush damage.
glossary.Rush: This unit may attack on its deployment turn if ready. Moving normally still exhausts it; Rush does not grant extra actions.
glossary.Mobile: The first move this unit makes each turn does not exhaust it. The move still costs a major action. Later moves exhaust normally.
glossary.Precision: This unit’s attacks cannot be redirected by a Guard. Defensive response Orders remain legal.
glossary.Berserk: This card gains +1 Attack while it has any damage.
glossary.Command aura: Other friendly battlefield cards in the same territory gain +1 Attack for each allied Command card there. The source does not boost itself.
glossary.Medic: At the start of its owner’s offensive turn, this card heals every friendly card in its territory by 1. Each Medic contributes; health cannot exceed printed maximum.
glossary.Retaliate: After a normal simultaneous combat, a defending Retaliate card that survived deals 1 non-combat damage to the surviving attacker. This happens after combat deaths. It cannot trigger from an Order, Ambush, Retreat, or another Retaliate hit.
glossary.Sabotage: An action Order suppresses all printed traits on one enemy permanent until that card’s owner next begins an offensive turn. It does not change printed stats, prevent actions, remove incoming allied auras, or cancel an already played Order. Suppression clears before Medic passives resolve.
glossary.Scavenge: When another ally here is destroyed, a surviving unsuppressed Scavenge source draws 1. All Scavenge sources and The Scavenger’s Nothing Wasted share one casualty draw per player per global turn. A nearby source takes priority; the Commander is the fallback.
glossary.Asset: A permanent support card that commits Presence and contributes to capture, but cannot move or declare attacks. Its passive traits remain active. It can be targeted and destroyed.
glossary.Unique: You may control only one copy of this card at a time. A replacement can deploy after the existing copy leaves the field.
glossary.Rally: Ready an exhausted friendly unit. Deployment-turn attack restrictions still apply; the next move or attack still costs an action.
glossary.Shield: A response Order that reduces combat damage to the defender for this combat only. It does not stop damage from Orders.
glossary.Ambush: A response Order deals damage to the attacker before combat. If that destroys the attacker, no combat damage is exchanged.
glossary.Retreat: A response Order moves the defender one territory toward its home, if the destination is legal and has room. The attacker exhausts and no combat damage is exchanged.
glossary.Counter: Cancel the defender’s response Order. Both Orders are spent and discarded; the original combat proceeds. There is no counter to a counter.
glossary.Disrupt: Add temporary enemy spending, capped at their currently available Presence. This can limit reactions now; their spending still resets at the start of their next offensive turn.
glossary.Reclaim: Return a friendly permanent to hand and free its committed Presence. Wounds stay on the returned card and remain after redeployment. Redeployment pays printed Capacity and Command Action costs.
glossary.Reserves: When a draw needs an empty deck, shuffle your discard/casualties into a new reserve deck. If both are empty, skip that draw. There is no fatigue damage.
glossary.Prototype lore: Leader names are editable generic roles. The reserved Riftwalker slot has no gameplay effect in Sprint 001.
glossary.Armor: Reduce incoming regular combat damage by 1 on any ground. Armor adds to Fortify on owned ground. Printed Armor and temporary Reinforce do not stack. Orders, Ambush and Retaliate bypass Armor; Sabotage suppresses printed Armor.
glossary.Mark: The marked enemy takes +1 damage from each positive incoming regular combat hit, including normal simultaneous return fire, until its next offensive turn starts. A zero-Attack card does not gain damage; shields and protection can absorb the bonus. Marks do not stack. Orders, Ambush and Retaliate gain no bonus.
glossary.Reinforce: Heal the chosen friendly permanent by the printed amount and give it temporary Armor 1 until your next offensive turn starts. Temporary Armor does not stack with printed Armor; it adds to Fortify on owned ground.
glossary.Adapt: Choose one printed mode when playing this Order. Only that mode resolves, with its usual target requirements. All modes pay this card’s printed Capacity and 1 Command Action; this is a choice, never a random result.
glossary.Capacity: Your army support limit. Available Capacity = total Capacity − committed Presence − temporary spending. Ordinary deployments spend no Command Action.
glossary.Command Actions: Three per offensive turn by default. Attacks, moves, tactical Orders and cards with an explicit command cost consume Command Actions. Ordinary deployments and low-impact support are Free Actions; responses and counters never consume a Command Action.
glossary.Free Action: An action that consumes zero Command Actions. It still requires sufficient Capacity, a legal location/target, and the usual timing restrictions.
glossary.Forced Retreat: After capture, displaced defenders resolve in ascending card UID order. A unit retreats one territory toward its home only into friendly-owned ground with a free allied slot. Wounds remain; forced retreat costs no resources and exhausts the unit until its next turn. Immobile assets, full/no friendly destinations and units at home are eliminated.
glossary.Frontline: Owned ground stays contiguous on both sides of one contested objective. Enemy forces may occupy the objective, but never remain stranded behind the moving frontline.
